simple.meaning: יוֹצָדָק (Yôwtsâdâq) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with priesthood and in connection with prophetic witness. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Ezra, Nehemiah, beginning at Ezra 3:2. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, family line, offering, altar, Torah, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יוֹצָדָק (H3136) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows יוֹצָדָק through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: יוֹצָדָק (Yôwtsâdâq) / H3136 is tracked through Ezra 3:2, Ezra 3:8, Ezra 5:2, Ezra 10:18. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak stood up with his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.

Now in the second year of their coming to God’s house at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and all those who had come out of the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of Yahweh’s house.
Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build God’s house which is at Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
Among the sons of the priests there were found who had married foreign women:
These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe.
